items.title: 63520_Ernie Fields oral history interview
items.q: Little Dick was sitting behind the steering wheel... Dick opened the door... Dick said, I'm driving it

ctx.x: bus any farther. He said I'll tow you down there after my partner comes back, but I can't leave now because there's nobody but me. So I said okay, I'll wait then. He said yes. So we went outside the station and I went in this little cafe part and asked the lady in there could we get service and she said yes and I said can we eat in here and she said why, sure. I guess she judged how many we were and she wasn't going to miss that nice treat and so before she said anything, I said can we wash up. You know how they…

So we went to the restroom to wash up and I told the men we could get service and so we ate, went back in the bus still waiting for this man to come back so the fellow could tow us down the road to this garage. Directly, a white guy came up, Little Dick was sitting behind the steering wheel, he hit on the door and Dick opened the door and he said, who's driving this tank? And you know he

talked so flat and everything, everybody looked around and Dick said, I'm driving it; better move this thing. Dick said we're waiting on the man, we're going to go to the garage. Who owns this tank? I said I own it. Well, you better move this bus. I said we got a little bus trouble, it can't run now; I said it can run, but I'm afraid we'll ruin the motor. I said I'm waiting on the mechanic, we're going to go down there about three miles. I'm telling you you got to move this thing. Now I work on the railroad with…
